title: Issue #205: [P0] Persist Aurora agent identity, revocation and task lifecycle across restart
content:
State: open

## Goal
Close the gap between registry/task primitives and a durable, recoverable runtime lifecycle.

## Scope
Use the normative identity/job contracts from the standards issue. Wire registry persistence into the caller/runtime; implement or verify durable task/run state, revocation, duplicate rejection and terminal state transitions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Agent registration is authenticated and IDs are unique; duplicate registration is rejected.
- [ ] Revocation/expiry is enforced at action time and survives restart.
- [ ] Registry and task/run state survive a supported process restart.
- [ ] Submission, queued, leased, running, retrying, cancelled, failed and completed transitions have explicit valid transitions.
- [ ] Tests cover corrupt/missing persistence, restart, duplicate IDs, revoked identity, timeout and retry.
- [ ] CI evidence references the exact tested commit SHA.

## Dependencies
Normative identity and compute-job contracts.

## Out of scope
This issue alone does not prove multi-node decentralization or production readiness.
